name: Enterprise Applications, Governance and Tools
blurb: What organisations actually do with AI and the rules that constrain it: industry use cases, security, law and compliance, litigation, prompt libraries, benchmarks, calculators, and downloadable working documents.

domains.name: Industry Use Cases
domains.blurb: What AI is actually used for, industry by industry, with ROI, vendors, risks, and case studies.

sections.name: Manufacturing
sections.blurb: Predictive maintenance, machine vision on the line, and generative design, with A3 automation data, IoT Analytics, and NIST standards work.

sections.name: Healthcare
sections.blurb: Imaging diagnostics, clinical documentation, and drug discovery, with the health-specific model benchmarks and KLAS and Rock Health tracking adoption.

sections.name: Retail
sections.blurb: Demand forecasting, recommendation, and customer-service automation at volume, with NRF, Coresight, and IHL tracking the deployments.

sections.name: Construction
sections.blurb: Computer-vision safety monitoring, BIM clash detection, and autonomous site scanning, sourced from AGC, BuiltWorlds, and the proptech and contech trackers.

sections.name: Legal
sections.blurb: Research, review, and drafting at scale, the citation-sanction lesson, and the benchmarks and trade bodies that measure legal AI accuracy.

sections.name: Accounting
sections.blurb: Transaction classification, audit anomaly detection, close automation, and the shift from sampling to full-population testing, with AICPA, IMA, and benchmark sources.

sections.name: Insurance
sections.blurb: Underwriting, claims triage, and fraud detection under active regulator supervision, with NAIC, AM Best, and the Evident insurance index.

sections.name: Banking
sections.blurb: Fraud detection and credit models are decades old; generative AI in service and compliance is the new frontier, under Fed SR 11-7 model risk supervision.

sections.name: Government
sections.blurb: Federal AI use inventories, GAO oversight, international readiness indexes, and the state legislatures writing AI law tracked on this site.

sections.name: Education
sections.blurb: Tutoring systems, drafting assistance, and academic integrity policy from K-12 through university, with market tracking and this site's own course catalog.

sections.name: Real Estate
sections.blurb: Automated valuation is the sector's oldest AI and now federally regulated under FHFA and CFPB quality-control rules; plus valuation, leasing, and property-management platforms with methodology disclosed.

sections.name: Hospitality
sections.blurb: Revenue management, service automation, and AI assistants as a booking discovery channel hotels now compete in, from Skift and AHLA to the distribution and restaurant tech vendors.

sections.name: Energy
sections.blurb: Grid optimisation, exploration, and the datacenter power crunch that makes energy both an AI user and AI's binding constraint, from EPRI and DOE to the utilities and oilfield majors.

sections.name: Transportation
sections.blurb: Autonomous driving is the visible front; AI also runs freight matching, maritime navigation, transit, and aviation, from IMO and EASA to the trucking, shipping, and aviation majors.

sections.name: Agriculture
sections.blurb: Vision-guided spraying, yield prediction, and autonomous equipment at commercial scale, tracked through USDA ERS, FAO, satellite data providers, and the equipment and standards bodies.

sections.name: Mining
sections.blurb: Autonomous haulage and ore-body modelling in the sector that automated early, from USGS exploration data and Earth MRI to Rio Tinto, Komatsu, KoBold, and the AI-native explorers.

sections.name: Defense
sections.blurb: Decision support, autonomy, and ISR processing as programs of record; DIU as the commercial on-ramp; free federal procurement data first, subscription analysts labeled.

sections.name: Media
sections.blurb: Generation tools transformed production while training-data litigation transformed the business relationship with AI; cross-linked to the lawsuit tracker.

sections.name: Sports
sections.blurb: Performance analytics, broadcast automation, and officiating assistance, from NCAA and NFHS governance to Hudl, Catapult, and the sports technology research network.

sections.name: Nonprofits
sections.blurb: Grant writing, donor analytics, and service delivery on small budgets, with governance capacity as the constraint, from CEP and NTEN to Candid and the equity project.

sections.name: Churches and Faith Organisations
sections.blurb: Sermon prep, administration, and pastoral limits across hundreds of thousands of congregations, from Barna research and faith-tech platforms to Notre Dame ethics work.

domains.name: AI Security and Risk
domains.blurb: Prompt injection, jailbreaks, model poisoning, supply chain attacks, data leakage, shadow AI, deepfakes, and the tooling that defends against them.

sections.name: Prompt Injection
sections.blurb: Direct and indirect prompt injection: how instructions hidden in content hijack model behavior, documented attacks, and current defenses.

sections.name: Jailbreaks
sections.blurb: Techniques that bypass model safety training, and how labs measure and patch against them.

sections.name: Model and Data Poisoning
sections.blurb: Corrupting training data or model weights to plant backdoors and biases, and the research on detecting it.

sections.name: AI Supply Chain Attacks
sections.blurb: Compromised models, datasets, and packages upstream: malicious model files, dependency attacks, opaque fourth-party model chains, AI bills of materials, and registry integrity.

sections.name: Data Leakage
sections.blurb: Training data extraction, membership inference, and models revealing what they should not.

sections.name: Model Theft
sections.blurb: Weight exfiltration and model extraction through APIs, and what providers disclose about protecting them.

sections.name: Shadow AI
sections.blurb: Unsanctioned AI use inside organizations: the exposure it creates and how enterprises detect and govern it.

sections.name: AI-enabled Malware
sections.blurb: What is documented, by primary sources, about AI-assisted malicious code and the vendor and government reporting on it.

sections.name: Deepfakes and Synthetic Identity
sections.blurb: Synthetic media fraud, identity spoofing, detection methods, and the laws responding to them.

sections.name: AI Phishing and Social Engineering
sections.blurb: How generated text and voice change phishing at scale, per published incident and vendor reporting.

sections.name: AI Security Tooling
sections.blurb: The defensive tooling landscape, organized by six security domains: Security Governance and Risk Management, Security Operations, Architecture and Engineering, Application and Product Security, Third-Party and Supply Chain Risk, and Data Protection and Privacy.

sections.name: Agent and Non-Human Identity
sections.blurb: The explosion of machine identities: agent credentials, delegated authority, revocation, and the lateral movement paths nobody is watching.

sections.name: AI Agent Security
sections.blurb: Agent kill chains, cascading multi-agent failure, circuit breakers, agent-to-agent trust boundaries, and runtime supervision of autonomous systems.

sections.name: AI in Security Operations
sections.blurb: Defending with AI: machine-speed investigation, human supervision models, automation bias, kill-switch protocols, and securing the SOC's own AI.

sections.name: AI Privacy and Data Protection
sections.blurb: The deletion problem in trained models, inference as data collection, memory sprawl, purpose enforcement, and cross-border inference.

sections.name: AI Red Teaming and Adversarial Evaluation
sections.blurb: Continuous adversarial testing of AI systems: methods, benchmarks, disclosure practices, and the evidence that earns expanded autonomy.

domains.name: AI Compliance, Law and Regulation
domains.blurb: State AI legislation and federal rulemaking, plus the 61 frameworks, standards, and enforcement records organisations are measured against: ISO 42001, the NIST AI RMF, the EU AI Act, SOC 2, the sector rules, and the agencies actually bringing cases.

sections.name: AI Laws by State
sections.blurb: Every tracked AI bill in all fifty states, DC, Puerto Rico, and Congress, one page per jurisdiction, refreshed daily from LegiScan.

sections.name: AI Governance Frameworks
sections.blurb: ISO 42001, the NIST AI RMF, the EU AI Act, SOC 2, the sector rules, and the agency enforcement records, explained in plain English.

sections.name: Federal AI Legislation
sections.blurb: Bills before Congress and federal rulemaking: 614 tracked congressional AI bills refreshed daily from LegiScan, 101 Federal Register documents from the rulemaking watch, the agency enforcement records (FTC, SEC, EEOC, CFPB, HHS OCR), and how existing federal statutes, HIPAA, FCRA, ECOA, COPPA, FERPA, GLBA, Title VII, the CFAA, apply to AI.

sections.name: Global AI Laws
sections.blurb: The EU AI Act, the EU Cyber Resilience Act and product liability regime, GDPR as applied to AI, DORA, NIS2, China's AI regulations, and the Council of Europe Framework Convention, explained in plain English with the compliance obligations each creates.

domains.name: AI Litigation
domains.blurb: Living case pages for AI lawsuits in United States courts, refreshed from the dockets daily.

sections.name: AI Lawsuit Tracker
sections.blurb: Living case pages for AI lawsuits in United States courts, with docket timelines refreshed daily from CourtListener. Every case is labeled by claim family: copyright, right of publicity, product liability and wrongful death, hiring discrimination, biometric privacy, securities fraud, trade secrets, platform access, patent, consumer protection, and government contracts.

domains.name: Prompt Engineering
domains.blurb: A working prompt library by business domain plus reference pages for the ten established prompting techniques, each with what it is, when it works, when it fails, and the paper behind it. 24 original templates with token estimates and model notes.

sections.name: Prompt Library
sections.blurb: Original working templates by business domain: sales, marketing, finance, coding, HR, cybersecurity, healthcare, and education, with token estimates and model compatibility notes.

sections.name: Prompt Techniques
sections.blurb: The established techniques, zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought, self-consistency, ReAct, tree of thoughts, RAG, prompt chaining, role prompting, and meta prompting, each with when it works, when it fails, and the source paper.

domains.name: Benchmarks and Performance
domains.blurb: Model, hardware, framework, vector database, and agent benchmarks: 18 tracked benchmarks, each with a plain statement of what it measures, what it does not, and where the live results are.

sections.name: Model Benchmarks
sections.blurb: What each benchmark measures and what it does not.

sections.name: Hardware Benchmarks
sections.blurb: GPU, CPU, and NPU throughput on real workloads.

sections.name: Framework and Inference Benchmarks
sections.blurb: Serving stacks compared under load.

sections.name: Vector Database Benchmarks
sections.blurb: Recall, latency, and cost at scale.

sections.name: Agent Benchmarks
sections.blurb: Task completion, reliability, and cost per solved task.

domains.name: AI Calculators and Interactive Decision Tools
domains.blurb: Six interactive estimators for the questions that decide whether an AI project is viable: token cost, GPU memory, context window fit, training cost, energy and carbon, and return on investment. Each shows its own arithmetic and states what it excludes.

sections.name: AI Calculators
sections.blurb: Six interactive estimators: token cost, GPU VRAM, context window fit, training cost, energy and carbon, and return on investment.
